question: What is the main goal of doing a secondary survey in critical care?

question: What is the main goal of the whole operating theatre team?

options.D: Maintaining hospital financial records and surgical supplies

question: What is the primary purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.B: Conducting clinical trials for newly discovered pharmaceutical drugs

options.D: Managing hospital budgets and staff shift rosters effectively

question: A young female patient has Chlamydia. What is the standard medical treatment?

options.A: A series of therapeutic vaccines given over a six-month recovery period

options.C: A course of oral antibiotics for the patient and treatment for her recent sexual partners
options.D: Surgical drainage of infected cervical cysts followed by topical anti-fungals

question: When checking a home for safety, which of these is a common physical hazard?

options.A: High white blood cell count
options.B: Elevated resting heart rate
options.C: Incorrect medication dosage
options.D: Loose floor rugs

question: A client with active breast cancer asks for an injectable contraceptive. How is this classified under WHO guidelines?

options.A: Category 4

question: What must a nurse always do before starting any care in a patient's home?

options.A: Publishing the care plan in a national newspaper
options.B: Receiving written approval from local community leaders
options.C: Consulting the hospital board of directors

explanation: Always! Respecting our patients means getting their clear okay before doing any checks or procedures. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T1#GNS324_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the normal heart rate range for a healthy adult in Normal Sinus Rhythm?

options.A: 100 to 120 beats per minute

question: Before you start collecting data for a community diagnosis, what is usually the very first step?

question: What is the primary function of the male accessory reproductive organs?

options.A: To store urine before it leaves the body
options.B: To produce and release immature sperm cells

question: A patient has a painful abscess right over the palm of their wrist, dangerously close to major nerves and blood vessels. What should you do first?

options.A: Apply hot compresses and send the patient home
options.B: Start high-dose oral antibiotics without any drainage
options.C: Immediately perform bedside incision and drainage
options.D: Refer the patient for specialized surgical evaluation

explanation: Hands and faces have delicate nerves and blood vessels. Abscesses in these tricky spots are best left to specialists to avoid accidental permanent injury. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T4#GNS311_U4_T4_h2)

question: What brings people together in a community of identity or orientation?

options.A: Working for the same commercial transport company
options.B: Living within the exact same municipal boundary line
options.C: Shared values, faith, culture, or life experiences
options.D: Sharing a temporary emergency shelter after a flood

explanation: You nailed it! It's heart and culture—beliefs, traditions, and life experiences—that bond these groups together, not just physical land. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is having a chain of command (hierarchical system) for hormones helpful for the body?

options.A: It prevents any possibility of hormone overproduction or toxicity
options.B: It allows a central brain region to coordinate widespread body responses
options.C: It eliminates the need for negative feedback loops in peripheral organs
options.D: It ensures that blood glucose levels remain entirely independent of brain activity

explanation: Having the brain act as the head office allows it to smoothly manage and coordinate multiple glands all over the body at once. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which cells in our bones are responsible for breaking down old bone tissue?

question: How does social stigma directly affect patients who need post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees faster recovery times inside the emergency ward

options.D: It improves the emotional rapport between nurses and patients

question: What do we call an infection that a patient picks up while receiving care in a hospital?

options.A: An allergic reaction to medication given during a surgical procedure

options.C: Any illness a person brings into the hospital from their home environment
options.D: An infection a patient catches while inside a medical facility for care

question: Which hormone is produced by the placenta to help maintain the corpus luteum and pregnancy in the early stages?

options.D: Thyroid-stimulating hormone

question: When reviewing literature, what do we call the missing or weakly studied areas in current research?

question: How do barrier methods of contraception primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By stopping the ovaries from releasing eggs

options.D: By physically blocking sperm from meeting the egg

question: Which hormone from the pituitary gland shoots up as the body approaches menopause?

options.D: Follicle-stimulating hormone

explanation: Think of the pituitary gland shouting louder (making more FSH) when the ovaries stop responding. Great revision point! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h2)

question: A patient is feeling very carsick on a bus ride. Which receptors should an effective anti-nausea drug target?

options.A: Opioid and cannabinoid

options.C: Serotonin and dopamine

question: Why must a patient return 48 to 72 hours after getting a Mantoux injection?

options.A: To ensure the PPD liquid does not leak out of the skin layers

options.C: To allow enough time for the delayed immune reaction to peak

question: A nurse notices that a disinfectant storage room has no windows or airflow. What immediate danger does this pose?

options.A: Rapid growth of bacterial spores inside the closed storage containers

options.C: Immediate freezing of all liquid disinfectants stored on the shelves
options.D: Accumulation of harmful chemical fumes leading to staff respiratory irritation

explanation: Good catch! Without proper ventilation, strong chemical vapors build up in the air and can make nursing staff very sick when they breathe them in. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h7)

question: A patient with severe malaria isn't getting better despite finishing a full course of drugs bought from an unverified roadside vendor. What should you suspect?

question: Which specific questionnaire is widely used to screen mothers for postpartum depression?

question: What is the main purpose of secondary prevention?

options.D: Creating broad national economic health policies

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching issues early through screening before severe symptoms take over. Spot it early, treat it early! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h3)

question: What is a major risk if a patient with severe vulvitis keeps scratching the itchy area?

options.C: Complete closure of the vaginal canal
options.D: Secondary bacterial infection through broken skin

question: A nurse treats an unemployed mother whose children are malnourished and out of school due to financial hardship. What is the best immediate action for the nurse to take?

options.C: Wait until her physical health deteriorates further

question: Why does a nurse ask about other body systems when a patient comes in with joint pain?

options.C: It replaces the need to ask about the patient's current medications

question: What should you do right after the AED delivers a shock?

question: Why is a continuous flow of saliva important for maintaining oral health?

question: How do tough economic pressures and daily security worries affect mental health at home?

question: What does 'vicarious liability' mean for you as a nurse?

question: What is the main benefit of competency-based training over normal classroom lectures for PAC nurses?

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the gut?

question: Why might a bright, gifted child suddenly get poor grades on school tests?

question: Which of these is a core nursing responsibility when providing family planning supplies?

question: What is the main purpose of a low-calorie diet?

question: Why is a CT scan particularly useful for musculoskeletal disorders?

question: A nurse in a busy rural clinic runs out of sterile gloves during an emergency wound dressing. What is the safest clinical action?

question: As a nurse, what is the main goal of gender-transformative healthcare?

question: Which fungal infection is a major cause of meningitis in patients with advanced HIV/AIDS seen in Nigerian hospitals?

question: Why is the Chain of Survival compared to a linked chain?

question: What is the primary job of the Dorsal Respiratory Group in the medulla?

question: Which of the following is a core component checked during a psychosocial evaluation?

question: In Nigeria, what color of bin liner is normally used for ordinary, non-hazardous general waste?

question: How can you best support parents whose baby is in Gallows traction?

question: What is the primary function of planning in nursing management?

question: Which part of the nervous system controls the built-in (intrinsic) defecation reflex?

question: What is the main benefit of using a team-based structure in a workplace?

question: What term describes the official power attached to a management role that lets you give orders and make decisions?

question: A patient develops a bone infection in the foot after stepping on a nail while wearing sneakers. Which organism is most likely involved?

question: Why are breast self-exams and nurse checks so vital in community settings with limited resources?

question: What is the main job of the climbing fibers as they enter the cerebellar cortex?

question: What is a drug idiosyncrasy?

question: What key nursing action should you provide all through a teenager's labor?

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe infection control practice during specimen collection?

question: Why should nurses use open-ended questions when talking to a child about an injury?

question: What is the main purpose of a health referral system?

question: Why is nitrofurantoin great for a simple bladder infection, but not for a deeper kidney infection?

explanation: To see what your body burns at absolute rest, we need digestion and recent activity completely out of the picture. An overnight fast does the trick! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h2)

question: Why must nurses stress to parents the importance of finishing a child's entire course of antibiotics?

options.A: To prevent the child from developing a skin rash
options.B: To permanently boost the child's daily appetite
options.C: To completely wipe out the bacteria and prevent relapse
options.D: To ensure the child gains healthy weight rapidly

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early just because the child 'looks better' can let hidden bacteria bounce back and cause more kidney damage. Patient education at its finest! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h9)

question: What simple comfort measure can a nurse suggest for a patient experiencing mild fibroid cramps?

options.A: Applying a heating pad to the lower abdomen
options.B: Drinking large quantities of ice-cold water
options.C: Lying completely flat on the back for hours
options.D: Engaging in high-impact aerobic exercise

explanation: Heat helps relax the tight uterine muscles, offering a wonderful, drug-free way to soothe mild cramping. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of a gastrostomy feeding tube?

options.A: To deliver nutrition directly into the stomach
options.B: To provide continuous intravenous hydration
options.C: To bypass the small intestine during digestion
options.D: To remove excess air and fluid from the bowel

explanation: A gastrostomy tube places food and fluids straight into the stomach, bypassing the mouth and esophagus for patients who cannot swallow safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: What special food product is lifesaver for treating severe malnutrition in emergencies?

options.A: High-sodium carbonated soft drinks
options.B: Ready-to-use therapeutic foods (RUTF)
options.C: Frozen commercial beef burgers
options.D: Standard multi-vitamin tablet bottles

explanation: RUTFs (like nutrient-packed peanut pastes) don't need water or refrigeration, making them perfect for quickly nursing severely malnourished children back to health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h6)

question: A patient hasn't been able to hit their strict diet targets over the past month. What should you do?

options.A: Modify the unrealistic goal into smaller, more manageable steps
options.B: Discontinue all dietary counselling because the patient is non-compliant
options.C: Scold the patient for failing to follow professional medical advice
options.D: Increase the strictness of the meal plan to force compliance

explanation: Spot on! If a goal is too tough, we don't give up—we team up to break it down into smaller, easier steps. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h7)

question: Why is double-checking (validating) your data such an important step in assessment?

options.A: It is required by law to be completed within fifteen minutes of admission
options.B: It allows the nurse to delegate all future care tasks to unlicensed staff
options.C: It ensures your information is correct before you make clinical choices
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any subjective patient interviews

explanation: Validating helps you catch mix-ups or misunderstandings early, so you don't build a care plan on the wrong information. Always good to double-check! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T7#GNS123_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which specific detail about a suspected drug is critical to include on an ADR form so regulators can trace the manufacturing lot?

options.A: Shipping company
options.B: Factory location
options.C: Batch number
options.D: Advertising agency

explanation: The batch number lets regulators check if a bad reaction is happening because of a flaw in one specific manufacturing batch of the medicine. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of primary data collection?

options.A: Reviewing old hospital admission registers in the record room
options.B: Conducting house-to-house surveys and interviews with residents
options.C: Reading national census reports published ten years ago
options.D: Downloading international World Health Organization PDF reports

explanation: Primary data is gathered directly from the source by the healthcare worker conducting the investigation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h3)

question: What happens in passive surveillance?

options.A: Patients must call a special hotline to report their own illness.
options.B: Health workers actively visit every household in the village.
options.C: Data is only collected during a national census every ten years.
options.D: Clinics send routine reports without being pushed by health officers.

explanation: Think of passive surveillance as your local clinic doing what they normally do—sending in their regular reports as part of daily duty without waiting for someone to chase them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h3)

question: Why is knowing a drug's class super helpful when you meet an unfamiliar medication on the ward?

options.A: It tells the nurse the exact room temperature for storing the drug
options.B: It guarantees the patient will not experience any adverse reactions
options.C: It gives immediate clues about expected effects and side effects
options.D: It eliminates the need to check the hospital dosage calculations

explanation: Drugs in the same family share similar actions and side effects. Once you know the class, you already know a lot about how it behaves! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h1)

question: What does 'growth faltering' look like on a child's growth chart?

options.A: A steady upward curve parallel to reference lines
options.B: Measurements that stay above the median line
options.C: A sudden increase in height over one month
options.D: A flat or downward-sloping growth curve

explanation: Growth faltering happens when weight gain slows down or stops entirely, making the growth line flatten out or dip downwards. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h6)
